title: 8 Best Debt Management Software Tools in 2026
summary: Compare the 8 best corporate debt management software tools in 2026, from DebtBook and Kyriba to AI agents like Concourse, by debt coverage, compliance, and fit.
body_markdown:
Managing an organization's own debt, its loans, credit facilities, and bonds, and the schedules, covenants, and interest that come with them, is detailed, high-stakes work. Miss a covenant test or a payment date and the consequences are real. Debt management software centralizes debt instruments, automates amortization and interest calculations, tracks covenants and maturities, and produces the debt and compliance reporting finance and treasury teams need.


One note up front: "debt management software" is also a consumer term for debt-payoff and settlement apps. This guide is about *corporate and organizational* debt management, software for companies, governments, and institutions to manage the debt they owe. It spans three groups that rarely compete head to head: public-sector and nonprofit debt tools, enterprise treasury suites with debt modules, and borrower-side loan-portfolio platforms, plus the newer wave of AI agents. Here are the eight best corporate debt management software tools in 2026.


## **What is the best debt management software?**


> The best corporate debt management software in 2026 is Concourse for teams that want AI agents to track and report on debt across their systems, DebtBook for government, higher-education, and nonprofit debt, SymPro for public-sector debt and investment, Kyriba and GTreasury for enterprise treasury with integrated debt, ION Treasury for the most complex global treasuries, FIS for front-to-back treasury and risk, and LoanBoss for borrower-side commercial real estate debt.


> **Concourse is the AI-agent option on this list.** Instead of a system you maintain debt schedules in, Concourse deploys autonomous finance agents that connect to your ERP, banks, and source systems and do the work, tracking debt schedules and covenants, calculating interest and amortization, monitoring maturities, and assembling debt and liquidity reporting, with every figure traceable to source and a person approving.


## **How we evaluated debt management software**


Debt management software is not one market; a city treasurer, a multinational CFO, and a real-estate borrower need very different tools. We compared these across the criteria that change the decision:


- **Debt instrument coverage.** Loans, lines of credit, bonds, leases, and derivatives, and how complex an instrument the tool can model.
- **Schedules and calculations.** Amortization, interest, rate caps, and defeasance handled automatically versus in spreadsheets.
- **Covenant and maturity tracking.** Whether the tool monitors covenants and upcoming maturities and alerts you.
- **Reporting and compliance.** Debt reporting, and for the public sector, GASB compliance.
- **Treasury breadth.** Whether debt is standalone or part of a wider treasury suite with cash, FX, and investments.
- **AI capability.** From spreadsheet replacement to AI agents that track and report on debt.

## **The 8 best debt management software tools in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for AI Agents That Track and Report Debt**


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. Rather than a system you maintain debt schedules in, it connects to your ERP, banks, and source systems and does the work: tracking debt instruments and their schedules, calculating interest and amortization, monitoring covenants and upcoming maturities, and assembling debt and liquidity reporting, on a schedule or on demand.


What sets it apart from a treasury module is the execution model and the reach. Concourse does not just store your debt data; its agents pull from source systems, run the calculations, and prepare the reporting, and every figure traces back to source and is validated against evals built for your business, which makes it defensible. It meets teams where they work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and connects to 100+ systems including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, and Stripe. Concourse reports customer results including a 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per user per month, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. See our guides to[liquidity management](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/liquidity-management) and the[treasury management system](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/treasury-management-system) for the wider context.


**Best for.** Teams that want AI agents to track debt schedules and covenants and produce debt reporting across their systems, with full traceability.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse runs the debt tracking and reporting work; it is not a full enterprise treasury suite with front-office dealing and derivatives. Many teams run Concourse alongside a TMS, or as a lighter alternative to spreadsheets.


### **2. DebtBook (now Monetary), Best for Government, Higher-Ed, and Nonprofit Debt**


DebtBook,[now rebranded as Monetary](https://monetaryhq.com/) , is cloud software for debt, lease, and subscription management built specifically for government, higher-education, healthcare, and nonprofit finance teams, centralizing debt schedules, amortization, and GASB 87/96 compliance reporting. Founded in 2019, it is based in Charlotte, North Carolina.


**Best for.** State and local government, universities, health systems, and nonprofits that need debt and lease management with GASB compliance.


**Keep in mind.** It is purpose-built for the public and nonprofit sector; it is not a fit for corporate treasury or multinationals with FX and derivatives needs.


### **3. SymPro, Best for Public-Sector Debt and Investment**


SymPro is a long-standing public-sector treasury suite with a dedicated debt-management module alongside investment and cash management, used by municipalities, counties, and special districts to replace spreadsheets and legacy systems. Founded in 1985, it is now[part of Emphasys Software, owned by Constellation Software](https://sympro.com/about/) .


**Best for.** Municipalities, counties, special districts, and public treasurers managing debt and investments.


**Keep in mind.** It is focused on public-sector fixed income and comparatively legacy; a corporate treasury wanting modern payments, FX, and real-time bank connectivity will find it narrow.


### **4. Kyriba, Best for Enterprise Treasury With Integrated Debt**


Kyriba is a market-leading cloud treasury management system whose suite spans cash and liquidity, payments, FX, and a debt-and-investment module, with analytics and bank connectivity. In 2019,[Bridgepoint acquired a majority stake at a reported $1.2 billion valuation](https://www.pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2019/private-equity-treasury-management-acquisition/) .


**Best for.** Large and multinational corporates that want debt managed inside a full enterprise treasury platform.


**Keep in mind.** It is a broad platform where debt is one module; it can be heavy and costly for teams that only need debt-schedule and covenant tracking.


### **5. GTreasury, Best for Enterprise TMS With Debt Workflows**


GTreasury is an integrated treasury management system that consolidates balances and transactions across banks and ERPs, with debt, investment, derivatives, and hedging workflows. Founded in 1986, it was[acquired by Ripple for $1 billion in 2025](https://www.pymnts.com/acquisitions/2025/ripple-acquires-treasury-management-systems-supplier-gtreasury-for-1-billion) .


**Best for.** Mid-to-large corporates and global treasuries that want debt within a full TMS.


**Keep in mind.** Now owned by Ripple, expect a roadmap tilt toward stablecoins and tokenized assets, a strategic consideration for more conservative treasuries.


### **6. ION Treasury, Best for the Most Complex Global Treasuries**


ION Treasury serves the largest, most complex organizations, central banks, and government debt-management offices, with advanced multi-asset, multi-entity debt processing across a portfolio of products including its[Wallstreet Suite](https://iongroup.com/press-release/treasury/ion-introduces-wallstreet-suite-empowering-treasury/) .


**Best for.** The largest corporates, central banks, and government debt-management offices.


**Keep in mind.** It is aimed at the top of the market; implementation complexity and cost make it overkill for mid-market debt books, and ION sells several overlapping products, so selection matters.


### **7. FIS, Best for Front-to-Back Treasury and Risk**


FIS Treasury and Risk Manager, in its Quantum and Integrity editions, is an enterprise treasury and risk platform covering cash forecasting, market and credit risk, and debt and investments, including loan servicing, amortization, revolving facilities, and bond issuances, with integrated hedge accounting. It is part of[FIS (Fidelity National Information Services)](https://www.fisglobal.com/products/fis-treasury-and-risk-manager-quantum-edition) , one of the largest financial-technology companies.


**Best for.** Large, complex enterprises and financial institutions that need debt alongside full treasury and risk.


**Keep in mind.** It is enterprise-scale and feature-dense; smaller teams typically do not need the full risk and derivatives breadth.


### **8. LoanBoss, Best for Borrower-Side Commercial Real Estate Debt**


LoanBoss is borrower-side debt management for commercial real estate: it centralizes loan data and automates complex calculations like interest, rate caps, and defeasance, plus maturity and covenant monitoring. It[launched in 2020](https://www.prweb.com/releases/loanboss_launch_is_a_game_changer_for_real_estate_professionals/prweb16817611.htm) and is based in Charlotte, North Carolina.


**Best for.** Commercial real estate firms, REITs, private equity, and developers managing a portfolio of property loans.


**Keep in mind.** It is built for borrowers, not lenders, and specialized to commercial real estate; it is not a general corporate treasury debt tool.


*Also worth a look:* enterprise lenders managing loans they issue use servicing platforms like Finastra, nCino, or Lenvi, a different job from managing your own debt, and treasury newcomers such as Treasury4 are building dedicated corporate debt modules worth watching.


## **Types of debt management software**


"Debt management software" covers several different buyers. The main types for organizations managing their own debt:


- **Public-sector debt tools** manage municipal and institutional debt with GASB-compliant reporting (DebtBook, SymPro).
- **Enterprise treasury suites** fold debt and investment management into a full TMS with cash, FX, and payments (Kyriba, GTreasury, ION, FIS).
- **Borrower-side loan-portfolio platforms** manage a book of loans for real estate and asset-heavy borrowers (LoanBoss).
- **Spreadsheets** , still the default for many smaller teams, until the debt book and covenant tracking outgrow them.
- **AI agents** track debt schedules and covenants and assemble reporting across systems, rather than storing it in one more platform.


## **Which debt management software is right for you?**


There is no single best debt management software, only the best fit for your organization type and the debt you carry.


- **Choose Concourse** if you want AI agents to track debt schedules and covenants and produce debt reporting across your systems, with every figure traceable.
- **Choose DebtBook or SymPro** if you are in government, higher education, or the nonprofit sector.
- **Choose Kyriba or GTreasury** if you want debt inside a full enterprise treasury suite.
- **Choose ION Treasury** if you are among the largest or most complex global treasuries.
- **Choose FIS** if you need debt alongside deep treasury and risk management.
- **Choose LoanBoss** if you are a commercial real estate borrower managing a loan portfolio.


The 2026 shift is the same one reshaping the rest of finance: from systems you maintain debt data in to AI agents that track the schedules and covenants and produce the reporting for you.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best debt management software?**


It depends on your organization. DebtBook and SymPro lead for the public and nonprofit sector, Kyriba, GTreasury, ION, and FIS for enterprise treasury, and LoanBoss for commercial real estate borrowers. For teams that want AI agents to track debt and produce reporting across their systems with full traceability, Concourse is the strongest AI-agent option.


### **Is this the same as consumer debt management software?**


No. Consumer debt management software helps individuals pay down or settle personal debt. This guide covers corporate and organizational debt management: software for companies, governments, and institutions to manage the loans, bonds, and credit facilities they owe, including schedules, covenants, and compliance reporting.


### **What does corporate debt management software do?**


It centralizes an organization's debt instruments, automates amortization and interest calculations, tracks covenants and upcoming maturities, and produces debt and compliance reporting. For the public sector it also handles GASB lease and subscription accounting. The goal is to replace error-prone spreadsheets and never miss a covenant test or payment.


### **How is an AI agent different from debt management software?**


Traditional debt management software gives you a system to store debt data and run calculations in. An AI agent platform like Concourse does the work across your existing systems, pulling debt data from source, calculating interest and amortization, monitoring covenants, and assembling reporting, with a human approving. One is a place to keep the data; the other performs the tracking and reporting.


## **The bottom line**


Corporate debt management software ranges from public-sector debt tools to enterprise treasury suites to borrower-side loan platforms, and the right one depends on whether you are a government, a multinational, or a real-estate borrower. DebtBook and SymPro anchor the public sector, Kyriba, GTreasury, ION, and FIS the enterprise, and LoanBoss the commercial real estate world.


The bigger shift is from systems you maintain debt data in to AI agents that track the schedules and covenants and produce the reporting for you.
